title: Order-parameter-dependent mobility in the Convective-Viscous Cahn-Hilliard equation
authors: P. O. Mchedlov-Petrosyan, L. N. Davydov, O. A. Osmaev
abstract: Generally the mobility in the Cahn-Hilliard equation may depend on the order parameter; this was evident already from the original derivation. However, explicit introduction of such dependence results in tremendous calculation difficulties, so the constant mobility approximation was commonly used. On the other hand, in several cases this dependence appeared to be crucial, so more realistic expressions were applied, usually positive powers or polynomials; still, for such dependencies only approximate and/or numerical solution exist. We consider 'reciprocal' linear and quadratic dependencies of mobility on the order parameter; for these dependencies exact traveling wave solutions are obtained. Even more, in a limited interval of the parameters reciprocal quadratic mobilities are rather good approximations to polynomial mobilities.
summary: This work analyzes the Convective-Viscous Cahn-Hilliard equation, focusing on the challenging case where the mobility depends on the order parameter. By restricting the mobility dependence to specific reciprocal forms, the authors successfully derive exact analytical solutions for the traveling wave fronts. This provides a significant theoretical advance over previous approximations, offering deeper insight into non-equilibrium phase separation dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex dynamics of phase transitions modeled by the Cahn-Hilliard equation when the mobility coefficient depends non-trivially on the order parameter.
main_result: Exact traveling wave solutions are obtained for specific reciprocal linear and quadratic dependencies of the mobility on the order parameter, providing analytical insights where numerical methods previously were required.
method: The authors employ the traveling wave ansatz ($z = x - vt$) and solve the resulting nonlinear partial differential equation by assuming a specific functional form for the derivative ($\partial u / \partial z$).
model_or_system: The system is governed by the Convective-Viscous Cahn-Hilliard equation, which models phase separation and transitions using an order parameter $w$. The complexity arises from the mobility term $ ar{M}(w)$ depending on $w$.
key_observables: Front velocity ($v$), the solution profile $u(x-vt)$, and the constraints on system parameters ($\kappa, v$).
important_parameters: The mobility dependence parameters ($	heta, \xi$) and the ratio of convective to diffusive terms ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to specific functional forms for mobility (reciprocal dependencies) to achieve exact analytical solutions, and it assumes the solution approaches constant values at infinity.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the governing equation and the difficulty of non-constant mobility. It then focuses on deriving and solving the traveling wave equation using specific mobility forms, leading to detailed analysis in appendices regarding parameter constraints and solution forms.
why_interesting: While focused on classical phase transitions, the mathematical techniques for solving nonlinear PDEs with complex, state-dependent coefficients are highly relevant to modeling non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems, such as domain wall motion or quench dynamics.
